scenarioSurface.capabilityName: Govern one authoring convergence round deterministically
scenarioSurface.scenarioName: Govern one deterministic convergence round over a candidate

input.text: one capability candidate, its declared scenario identities, and the round history already admitted

outcome.text: every deterministic conformance rule is evaluated, the findings bind into one normalized finding set, and the round disposition is ADVANCED, REPAIRABLE, or BLOCKED

scenarioSurface.notes:
An authoring model proposes meaning. It must never be asked to decide what the
  machine already knows exactly. This capability owns everything mechanically
  decidable about a capability candidate, so probabilistic review never spends a
  token deciding whether an operator exists.

  Every rule here was derived from the admitted estate by the same method: observe a
  pattern, search for counterexamples, prove causality with a fixed baseline probe,
  and only then state the invariant. Prevalence alone is not law.

  The governing distinction is closure, not cardinality. Six required ports and six
  declared bindings prove nothing if the six identities do not resolve to each other.
  Coverage counts. Closure resolves.

  A round emits bounded findings, never a verdict of "try again". Each finding names
  the artifact, the authority pointer, the rule, what was observed, what was expected,
  and the constraint any repair must honour. Repair is therefore a narrowing problem
  rather than a regeneration problem, and admitted authority is preserved untouched.

  An invented operator is not a failure. It is REPAIRABLE. Only a session that cannot
  legitimately make another move is BLOCKED. Every scenario admits and emits one
  shared authoring convergence record.

expected.value: exactly one execution authority per scenario

repairConstraint.value: Give this scenario exactly one owning execution authority.
Express the same meaning using only admitted operators without changing the scenario outcome.
Rename the operand to the admitted key for this operator without changing the meaning.

observed.template: expression-shaped discriminator "op" at {p} sits beneath a literal boundary

expected.value: literal data remains opaque to expression interpretation regardless of the fields present in the literal value

repairConstraint.value: Rename the field or restructure the literal so its value cannot be reinterpreted as an expression envelope. Valid domain data named "op" inside a literal must remain legal.
Under invoke-scenario composition the observed sequence is the root scenario alone.

observed.template: portId "{p}" resolves to no declared binding

repairConstraint.value: Use the exact portId declared in interfaces.authority.json portBindings, or declare that binding. Both must name the same port.

expected.value: exactly one edge realization: composition OR transitions, never both

repairConstraint.value: This capability composes scenarios with invoke-scenario, so set transitions to [].

observed.template: entry for declared port "{p}" supplies no output

expected.value: an entry keyed by a declared portId supplies the outcome that port produces

repairConstraint.value: Supply {"output": ...} for this port. Only the literal key "authority-driven-composition" may carry an authority reference.

providerQualification: Bindings are declared suppliers, not proof of live availability. Simulation requires explicit fixture/provider evidence.
